lesson_title: The Day the Taps Didn't Stop
hook_text: In 2018, four million people were told their taps were about to run dry, and then they did something remarkable.
clip_script: Cape Town, 2018. Three years of drought. The dams are almost empty. The city announces Day Zero, the day the taps will be turned off. So people change. Two-minute showers. Bath water saved to flush toilets. Gardens left brown. Leaks fixed. In a few years, the city's water use falls by about half. Day Zero never comes. That's the power of millions of small actions. The same idea works for the climate. Everything we do leaves a carbon footprint, from the coal-powered electricity in our homes to the food we waste and the way we travel. Switch off. Walk. Reuse. Waste less. But one family can't build a solar farm or a train line. That takes governments and companies too. Every hand counts.
visual_style: Cracked mud in an empty Cape Town dam; people queueing at a spring with water bottles; a timer next to a shower; a bucket of grey water by a toilet; a footprint made of smoke; a family switching off lights; a cyclist and a full bus; a solar farm.
pacing: Tense at the crisis, energetic during the actions, uplifting at the end.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to learn what individuals can do to use resources sustainably and lower their carbon footprint.
